dossier.public_summary: The dip looks very different on odd vs even orbits and changes depth strongly from sector to sector, including within the same TESS pipeline. That pattern matches a stellar binary seen at twice the folded period, not a steady planet transit on the target.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by >6 sigma with very different depths. This is the classic signature of an eclipsing binary at twice the period (21.8 d) where only the primary eclipses appear in odd events and the even events are much shallower/unrelated, not a planet.

Depth changes strongly between sectors and also within the same light-curve source (sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source, TESS-SPOC p_constant 0.00013758962301966136). A planet should have steady depth; large sector-to-sector and within-source variation favours a blended or stellar signal over a constant planet transit.
Independent scorer trained on follow-up outcomes rates this far below the median planet (0.5) and in the false-positive range, consistent with odd/even and depth variability.
